messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: CoreOperationTest.testEmptyNodeSetOperations asserts that evaluating the XPath expression "/idonotexist >= 0" must yield Boolean.FALSE. The left-hand side is an empty node-set because the path does not resolve to any nodes.
- XPath spec requirement (as summarized in the bug report): when comparing a node-set with a number, the comparison is true iff there exists at least one node in the node-set whose string-value, when compared to the number, satisfies the operator. For an empty node-set, there are no nodes, so the result must be false.

What the code does:
- CoreOperationRelationalExpression.computeValue delegates to compute(left, right), where left/right are the values of the operands (args[0], args[1]).
- compute(Object, Object) tries to implement the XPath semantics for node-set comparisons:
  - It first calls reduce on both operands:
    - reduce converts SelfContext to a single NodePointer, and a Collection into an Iterator. It does not convert null into an iterator.
  - It then handles node-set cases only when an operand is an Iterator:
    - If both are Iterators: findMatch iterates to see if any pair matches (string-based comparisons via recursion).
    - If one side is an Iterator: containsMatch iterates left/right to see if any single node matches against the scalar right/left, respectively.
  - If neither operand is an Iterator, it falls back to numeric comparison:
    - It converts both to doubles using InfoSetUtil.doubleValue and, if neither is NaN, applies the relational operator via evaluateCompare.

Where it goes wrong for empty node-sets:
- For a nonexistent path like "/idonotexist", the left operand’s computeValue returns nothing. Instead of being represented as an empty Iterator/Collection (which would lead to containsMatch(...) returning false as required), it ends up as null.
- reduce does not transform null into an Iterator, so the Iterator branches are skipped.
- The code then falls back to numeric comparison:
  - InfoSetUtil.doubleValue(null) is treated as a valid number (commonly 0.0), not NaN.
  - The right-hand side 0 becomes 0.0; 0.0 >= 0.0 evaluates to true via evaluateCompare in CoreOperationGreaterThanOrEqual.
- Result: The expression "/idonotexist >= 0" incorrectly returns true, causing the test to fail.

Summary of the root cause:
- CoreOperationRelationalExpression.compute relies on recognizing node-sets through Iterator/Collection types to apply the correct “exists a node that satisfies...” semantics.
- When a location path resolves to no nodes, the left operand is null rather than an empty Iterator/Collection. This bypasses the node-set comparison logic and incorrectly triggers numeric comparison where null is implicitly treated as 0.0, yielding the wrong result (true instead of false).
- The correct behavior would be to represent an empty node-set as an empty Iterator/Collection (or otherwise ensure that null in this context is handled as an empty node-set so that the node-set comparison logic runs and returns false).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
